title: Primary mouse hepatocyte isolation
protocol: Setup perfusion station by placing metal platform within glass chamber.
Run tubing through perfusion machine and clamp end of tubing with a large binder clip.
Attach butterfly needle to each port.
Place unclamped end of tubing in perfusion buffer and turn on perfusion machine.
Let buffer flow until coming out of each needle, then clamp each butterfly needle tubing.
Pause perfusion machine until ready to use.
Take anesthetized animal via IP injection of Avertin and place supine on metal platform.
Tape all limbs down.
Remove abdominal skin while preserving muscle and peritoneum.
Open peritoneum and abdominal cavity for full visualization of liver and abdominal organs.
Push stomach and intestines to the right side of animal.
Identify inferior vena cava (IVC) and portal vein (PV).
Cannulate IVC with butterfly needle ensuring bevel of needle is facing up.
Use hemostat to secure needle within IVC and tape tubing down to metal platform.
Unclamp butterfly needle tubing.
Turn on perfusion machine.
Immediately identify and cut the PV.
Pass at least 100 mL of perfusion buffer through a single mouse.
Add collagenase to the collagenase buffer and mix well while the perfusion is running.
Switch the tubing to the collagenase buffer and resume perfusion until the entire volume of collagenase buffer has been used.
Remove the liver by cutting along the vasculature and connective tissue, avoiding the liver parenchyma.
Place the liver in a petri dish with 10 mL of perfusion buffer.
Agitate the liver to dissociate the hepatocytes.
Transfer the dissociated cell suspension to a 70 micron mesh filter over a 50 mL Falcon tube using a serological pipette.
Complete the volume in the Falcon tube with perfusion buffer to dilute the collagenase.
Centrifuge the sample at a minimum speed of 800 rpm for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in washing media, then centrifuge again at 800 rpm for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant once more, resuspending the cells in 10 mL (or 5 mL if the cell pellet is small) of plating media.
Suspended in plating media, the hepatocytes will remain viable until plated.
Plate cells on a collagen-coated surface.
